abstract: Documented distributions reflect where organisms occur and where people look. Here we model the annual hazard of a first provincial record on a complete species-by-province-year risk set for 1,029 Chinese bird records (2002–2024), dated to discovery rather than publication. Publication-year dating inflates the effort hazard ratio from 1.305 to 1.788 and manufactures a spurious climate-variability effect. Corrected, accumulated warming relative to a species' historical range (1.362 per standard deviation) and survey effort (1.404) contribute comparably. Design-preserving permutation nulls centre warming on 1.157, not unity, an increment near 1.18, and collapse effort to 0.980 when its temporal alignment is broken. The largest variance component is a province-by-year random intercept (SD 0.804); effort's marginal return declines from 2.18 to 1.07 while the climate effect does not; and new records fall disproportionately east and northeast of species' ranges. Documented range gains therefore reflect climate and observation in roughly equal measure.

budget_check:
NEE hard limit: Introduction + Results + Discussion <= 3,600 words; abstract <= 150; main display items <= 6.

TEXT BUDGET. Source: Intro 672 + Results 6,246 + Discussion 833 = 7,751. Targets: Intro 430 + Results 2,220 + Discussion 780 = 3,430. Headroom 170 words (4.7%) against the 3,600 cap, deliberately reserved for the section-linking sentences and SI pointers that compression always adds back at copy-edit.

Results sum, section by section: 230 + 180 + 470 + 190 + 60 + 40 + 150 + 170 + 120 + 190 + 100 + 190 + 130 = 2,220, against the 2,400 brief. Under by 180, which is the real safety margin because Results is where a compressed draft rebounds.

WHERE THE 4,026 WORDS COME FROM. Four sections supply 2,880 of the 4,321 words cut from Results (67%): species and provinces 1,120 -> 150 (-970); nature reserves 775 -> 130 (-645); robustness 762 -> 190 (-572); migratory strategy 455 -> 40 (-415). None of the four is a protected conclusion, and all four are moved as intact blocks to SI rather than abbreviated in place. The remaining 1,441 words come from proportional trimming of the nine sections that do carry the protected conclusions. Intro contributes 242 and Discussion only 53 - Discussion is deliberately barely touched, because with Results at 36% of source length the Discussion is now the only place the four conclusions are stated in continuous prose.

PROTECTED CONCLUSIONS, WORDS ALLOCATED. (i) warming vs effort: 470 words, main Fig. 1 and main Table 1. (ii) province-by-year largest component: 190 + 60 = 250 words, main Fig. 3c. (iii) declining effort return, non-declining climate: 120 words in Results 9 plus a 1-sentence provincial-scale convergence in Results 7, main Fig. 3d. (iv) east / northeast bias: 170 words, main Fig. 4. Total 1,010 of 2,220 Results words (46%) go to the four protected conclusions, against 24% of the source. That is the intended shift: the compression is paid for by the supporting apparatus, not by the results.

NULL-MODEL CONSTRAINT. The 1.157 / about 1.18 / 0.980 qualification appears three times in the finished paper: in the abstract (25 of 147 words, 17%), inside the 470-word Results 3 block, and as the permutation-null-median column of main Table 1 with the explanatory table note preserved verbatim. It therefore survives even if a copy-editor deletes any one instance.

DISPLAY ITEMS. Source 27 (9 tables + 18 figure legends). Main: 5 figures + 1 table = 6, exactly at the cap, no slack. Every protected conclusion has at least one main-text display item, and Fig. 3 does double duty for (ii) and (iii), which is what makes 6 achievable. The 21 demoted items map to 10 Supplementary Notes, 10 Supplementary Tables and 16 Supplementary Figures (16 rather than 15 because main Fig. 11 is split, its order panels becoming Supplementary Fig. S16).

ABSTRACT. 147 words against the 150 cap, margin 3. Single paragraph, no citations, no subheadings, per NEE format. Fourteen numbers appear, all copied character-for-character from the source: 1,029 / 2002-2024 / 1.305 / 1.788 / 1.362 / 1.404 / 1.157 / 1.18 / 0.980 / 0.804 / 2.18 / 1.07. Note the abstract states the effort transition as 1.305 -> 1.788 whereas Results 2 states 1.788 -> 1.305; both digits are unaltered and both sentences are true, because the abstract describes what publication-year dating does to the corrected estimate and Results describes what re-dating does to the published one.

NUMBER VERIFICATION. Spot-checked against the results tables rather than the manuscript alone: tbl_null_models.csv gives N3 clim_change null median 1.15696 (= 1.157) and N2 effort null median 0.97957 (= 0.980); tbl_bootstrap_ci.csv gives the province cluster bounds 1.1957-1.7215 and 1.2075-1.7619 (= 1.20-1.72, 1.21-1.76) and the interaction 0.7416-0.9944 (= 0.74-0.99); tbl_change_decomposition.csv confirms S0 effort 1.78764 and S1 1.30508; tbl_v2_future_support.csv confirms 47.8 / 10.4 / 2.1 and 34.2 / 2.1 / 1.9. One inconsistency exists inside the source itself and I have not touched it: tbl_null_models.csv records the observed warming HR as 1.36604 while the manuscript and tbl_change_decomposition.csv S5 give 1.36165 (= 1.362). All retained text uses the manuscript value 1.362, per the rule that the source manuscript governs.

VERDICT. Within budget on all four NEE constraints, with margin on three (170 words of text, 3 words of abstract, 0 display items) and none on the fourth.
risks: Display items are at exactly 6 with zero slack. If a reviewer asks for any new main-text panel, something must be demoted, and the only demotable candidate is Fig. 5 (projection support) - which would leave the third Discussion pillar without a main display item. Decide in advance that Fig. 5 is the sacrificial slot rather than negotiating it under revision pressure.
